chunks: One of the firm decrees of Allah in the Wise Reminder (Qur'an), upon which He bestows reward and punishment, and through which He is pleased and displeased,
that it will not benefit a servant, even if he exerted himself and made his action sincere, if he leaves this world to meet his Lord with one of these characteristics without repenting from it:

that he associates a partner with Allah in what He has made obligatory upon him of worship, or appeases his anger by killing a person, or acknowledges a deed done by another, or seeks fulfillment of his needs from people by introducing an innovation in his religion, or meets people with a double face, or moves among them with a double tongue.
Understand this, for an illustration is a guide for its like.

key_terms.يَلْقَى النَّاسَ بِوَجَْيْنٍ: meets people with a double face (hypocrisy)
key_terms.يَمْشِيَ فِيهِمْ بِلِسَانَيْنِ: moves among them with a double tongue
key_terms.يُثِيبُ وَيُعَاقِبُ: He bestows reward and gives punishment

ai.seo_question: What are the specific sins or character flaws that invalidate a person's worship and sincerity according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) identifies specific 'decisive ordinances' (azaim) of God that invalidate worship if unrepented, highlighting that sincerity of action is insufficient without purity of creed and character. The text warns against subtle forms of hypocrisy, such as displaying religious innovation for social gain or maintaining a double-faced demeanor, which corrupt the individual's standing before God. This serves as a critical ethical framework in Shia scholarship, linking theological monotheism directly to social integrity and self-awareness.
